mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when GDP growth is positive, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity markets.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when unemployment is below 3%, more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production and housing starts indicate economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when both proxies rise, more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate in a tightening cycle may slow economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are positive when FEDFUNDS exceed 4%, more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment suggests economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when employment rises, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real consumer spending indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when RSAFS grows over 5%, more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation without corresponding unemployment increase may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are positive when CPI rises without UNRATE increase, more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production in late-cycle expansion supports positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when industrial production is strong, more than 35% of the time.
